newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC will proceed faster than WTO, says Manila.
newsitem.headline: APEC will proceed faster than WTO, says Manila.

text.p: Most members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum will make free trade commitments that go further than their promises to the World Trade Organisation, organisers of the forum's November 25 summit said on Tuesday.

"To everybody's surprise, we will find out that most countries are not really going to need the whole of 2020, some of them will be there by 2010," Philippine Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista told Reuters Financial Television.
APEC members have agreed that developed nations from the group will be completely free trade by 2010 while the poorer APEC countries reach that stage by 2020.

Bautista is the co-chairman of the APEC ministerial meeting which will start on November 22. The meeting precedes the annual one-day summit of APEC's 18 leaders in the nearby Subic Bay free port area.

At their two-day meeting, the ministers are expected to finalise their commitments on lowering trade and investment barriers in the region. After the meeting, the ministers will make their recommendations to their leaders in preparation for the November 25 summit.

"Some economies are even ahead in the schedule of their commitment in liberalisation. Indeed, the submissions went beyond (what was committed in) the Uruguay Round," foreign affairs undersecretary Federico Macaranas told a news conference.
He was referring to the last round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, which ended in 1994 and was replaced by the World Trade Organisation.

Bautista said the Philippines had agreed to bring down tariffs in all areas by 2004, excluding 10 agricultural products which it called sensitive. This was compared with its deadline of 2020 in the APEC timetable.

Bautista said the encouraging results came not from tough negotiations as was seen during the Uruguay Round, but because of the spirit of consensus within APEC. The consensus approach means that agreements are not binding but organisers of the summit said member economies would keep their promises.
"The character of the summit we try to build on is the climate of consensus, the climate of confidence with one another, the climate of building up trust on the whole process of APEC," Bautista said.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and the United States.
